# Independent audit: product-base continuation capacity

Source: `candidate 22d923b6274e7758`.

**Full PASS.** No repair is required.

For an arithmetic-centroid base, Jensen is applied at the SAME continuous
boundary point and normal across all fibers. Its integration is legitimate
with the actual boundary measure, including d=1 counting measure. A
base-independent continuation attains the N-fold lower bound. Thus the
result is an exact continuation-cost obstruction, not merely a dimensional
estimate or an unproved statement about a sampled point law.

At an exposed base, the finite exposing gap and a common bound on the
potential over all other measured boundary fibers make the displayed
positive-part potential vanish there. Positive part preserves convexity
because it is the maximum with zero; it is nonnegative and unchanged at
the chosen source boundary. The own-boundary lower bound proves optimality.

The finite capacity LP is correctly dualized. The constraint t_z>=0 gives
w_z<=1, t_z>=1+a.(z-p) supplies w_z>=0, and minimizing over unrestricted
a gives sum w_z(z-p)=0. Both primal and dual are feasible, bounded in
objective, and attain their values. The source point guarantees T>=1.
Its hinge at p equals one. Pointwise Jensen and nonnegativity establish
the lower bound for all convex continuations, and the constant-in-x
potential realizes it with exact cost TD.

One useful strengthening of the LOWER bound is immediate and does not
change the stated sharpness scope: for any prescribed nonnegative own
weight phi(n,x), including the nonconstant projective weight, the same
fixed maximizing w gives sum_z Psi(n,z,x)>=T(P,p) phi(n,x) pointwise.
Hence every continuation costs at least T(P,p)D. The source only asserts
general attainment for the arithmetic-centroid case, and T-attainment
for constant-in-x weights; this distinction is correct. Multiplying a
nonconstant phi by the minimizing base hinge is not generally jointly
convex, so no further attainment claim follows.

The note correctly retains all additional-fiber cap credits. It rules
out a denominator-only parity estimate, not a geometric payment or OC.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
